project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas Oenothera visual breadth module
project_scope.note: The canonical set spans both classic primrose and former-Gaura forms, making it unusually good for teaching family variation.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Look below the petals. The ovary sits beneath the sepals/petals/stamens, commonly with an obvious floral tube above it.
family_diagnostics.floral_pattern: Usually 4 sepals + 4 petals + 4 or 8 stamens in the local Oenothera set; stigma commonly 4-lobed.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Can be a many-seeded dehiscent capsule or a hard few-seeded indehiscent fruit in former-Gaura lineages.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Inferior ovary + floral tube + repeated 4-part architecture beats flower color every time.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: This family is perfect for learning that one structural plan can produce wildly different-looking flowers.

steps.title: 1 · Learn the classic primrose form
steps.look_for: Four broad petals arranged radially, with a conspicuous 4-lobed stigma.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows the easy-to-recognize classic Onagraceae form.

steps.title: 2 · Look below the petals
steps.look_for: An extraordinarily long floral tube leading down to the ovary below the flower.
steps.why_it_matters: Makes inferior ovary + hypanthium impossible to miss.

steps.title: 3 · Break the 8-stamen rule
steps.look_for: The same 4-part flower plan but only four stamens.

steps.title: 4 · Learn the former-Gaura form
steps.look_for: Petals held mostly to one side with long exserted stamens.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows that Onagraceae is not always radially symmetric.

steps.title: 5 · Follow flower to hard fruit
steps.look_for: A hard few-seeded 4-lobed fruit rather than a typical opening capsule.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit architecture is the second major axis of variation in the family.

comparisons.title: Onagraceae vs Lythraceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have 4-merous flowers and a floral cup. Onagraceae has an inferior ovary; Lythraceae is usually superior.

comparisons.title: Classic vs former-Gaura Oenothera
comparisons.rule: Classic forms are often radial with showy 4-petaled flowers and many-seeded capsules; former-Gaura forms may be one-sided with exserted stamens and hard few-seeded fruit.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not use flower color as the family ID; local species can be yellow, pink, white, or white aging pink/red.
